COPPER SURGES TO ALL-TIME HIGH Copper hit a record $14,533 a ton on the London Metal Exchange, fueled by fears of potential US tariffs on refined copper imports. Prices have jumped 17% over the past year, supported by tight mine supply and rising demand from data centers, renewable energy and power grids. Heavy shipments to the US have also reduced availability elsewhere, adding further pressure to prices.

IRAN’S OIL REVENUES COLLAPSE AS BLOCKADE TIGHTENS Iran’s oil income is rapidly shrinking as a US naval blockade restricts exports and offshore stockpiles fall. Iranian crude stored outside the Gulf has dropped from 90 million to 29 million barrels, while shipments to China are dwindling. With oil funding roughly a third of Iran’s state budget, the squeeze is worsening inflation, weakening the rial and pushing the economy deeper into crisis.

TRUMP CALLS FOR BAN ON BOMBARDIER SALES IN US President Trump called for Bombardier sales in the US to stop, accusing Canada of unfairly restricting American companies, including Gulfstream Aerospace. He argued that Bombardier depends heavily on American customers while Canada limits US businesses. Trump demanded that companies seeking access to the US market build in America, ending his message with a renewed “America First” push.

TRUMP WANTS TO RENAME NEW MEXICO “NEW AMERICA” President Trump has called for New Mexico to be renamed “New America,” sharing several altered maps on social media. New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham rejected the idea, saying the state’s historic name “isn’t up for debate.” Trump has previously pushed other geographic name changes, including Lake Ontario to “Lake America” and the Gulf of Mexico to “Gulf of America.”

OPENAI’S TOP SCIENTIST WARNS AI MAY BE MOVING TOO FAST OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is calling for “extreme caution” as AI capabilities rapidly advance. He warns that models could soon improve themselves without human intervention, making them increasingly difficult to understand and control. Pachocki expects AI labs to voluntarily slow development until shared safety standards are established, even as investment in self-improving AI accelerates.

IRAN ACCUSES CANADA OF BOWING TO U.S. PRESSURE Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei accused Canada of yielding to U.S. “intimidation” after Ottawa criticized Tehran over regional security and freedom of navigation. Baghaei said Canada was supporting what Iran views as U.S. military aggression and economic pressure. IRGC CLAIMS CAPTURE OF U.S. UNMANNED SUBMARINE Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claims it captured a U.S. unmanned submarine near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said the operation relied on intelligence and operational planning, describing the vessel as an advanced autonomous submarine that entered U.S. service in 2025. Iran said the submarine remains in its possession and that images will be released later. The claim has not been independently verified.

Ross said traders are concentrating positions in the next three to six months and becoming more selective about derivatives risk. KREMLIN HOPES US-BROKERED UKRAINE TALKS RESUME SOON The Kremlin says it hopes US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine will restart soon, after negotiations stalled in February. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to discuss possible terms of a settlement. His comments came after Presidents Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump spoke by phone Tuesday about prospects for ending the war in Ukraine.

KREMLIN: EUROPE FEELING PAIN OF HIGHER GAS PRICES The Kremlin says Europe is suffering from soaring natural gas prices amid the Iran war and could cut costs by buying Russian gas. European gas prices recently reached their highest level since late 2022. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Europe was hurting itself by relying on expensive spot-market gas instead of cheaper Russian supplies.

PIMCO: HIGH BOND YIELDS CHALLENGE STOCKS PIMCO says bonds are becoming more attractive after global yields climbed to their highest levels in more than a decade. US aggregate bond yields are now around 5%, roughly matching equity earnings yields. PIMCO argues bonds can once again provide meaningful income and protection if growth weakens, making a more balanced mix of stocks and fixed income increasingly attractive.

IRAN EXPANDS MARITIME RESTRICTED ZONE Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said a new maritime restricted zone will extend from Chabahar into parts of the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea, with exact coordinates to be announced. The move follows Tehran’s earlier plans to establish restrictions beyond the Strait of Hormuz, potentially widening disruption to shipping across a critical global energy route.

US MORTGAGE DEMAND FALLS AS RATES HIT 6.85% US mortgage applications fell 2.7% last week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. Refinancing applications dropped 6.2%, while home-purchase applications slipped 0.2%. The average 30-year mortgage rate rose six basis points to 6.85%, adding further pressure on borrowers and the housing market.

IRGC: WE WILL HIT 20 TARGETS FOR EVERY 2 OR 3 STRUCK Iran’s Revolutionary Guards warned they would respond forcefully to further attacks, saying every two or three Iranian targets hit could trigger strikes on 20 enemy targets. The IRGC also demanded an end to hostilities, an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, an end to Yemen’s blockade and the release of $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets.

U.S. BANK LAUNCHES ITS OWN STABLECOIN U.S. Bank has successfully tested USBDC, its proprietary dollar-backed stablecoin, in a live cross-border payment between its North American and European operations. The transaction ran on the Stellar blockchain while remaining integrated with the bank’s compliance and risk systems. U.S. Bank is exploring stablecoin applications including 24/7 payments, liquidity management, cross-border treasury operations and faster settlement.

CENTRAL BANKS FOCUS ON FUEL PRICES AS INFLATION RISK Central banks are increasingly watching refining margins, or “crack spreads,” as fuel shortages push gasoline and diesel prices higher. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said refined fuel prices may provide a better inflation signal than crude oil alone. AI BOOM DRIVES S&P 500 EARNINGS HIGHER S&P 500 earnings estimates are rising sharply, fueled by AI investment and stronger-than-expected corporate results. About 86% of companies beat analyst expectations, the highest share since 2021. Wall Street now expects 32% earnings growth in 2026, up from 24% before second-quarter results. AI-linked companies including Alphabet and Amazon delivered major beats, while communication services, consumer stocks and energy also saw significant upgrades.

AAPL - APPLE SET TO UNVEIL $2,000+ FOLDABLE IPHONE Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone Wednesday, marking new CEO John Ternus’ first major product launch. The device could cost more than $2,000, making it Apple’s most expensive handset yet. IDC expects Apple to capture 40% of the foldable smartphone market by end-2027. Apple is also expected to delay cheaper iPhone updates until spring, focusing this launch on the foldable, Pro and Pro Max models.

NORTHWESTERN MUTUAL: HOT CPI COULD TRIGGER FED HIKE Northwestern Mutual’s Matt Stucky says hotter-than-expected inflation could increase the chances of a Fed rate hike this month. Markets currently see roughly a 50-50 chance of a hike. Friday’s core CPI is expected to rise 0.2% month-over-month. A stronger reading, combined with the resilient U.S. labor market, could push the Fed toward tightening as policymakers focus on persistent inflation.

KUWAIT OFFERS OIL TRANSFERS OUTSIDE HORMUZ Kuwait Petroleum Corp is offering ship-to-ship transfers of crude oil and refined fuels outside the Strait of Hormuz as buyers avoid ports inside the waterway due to U.S.-Iran war risks. KPC says vessels will continue passing through Hormuz when conditions are safe. Kuwait’s naphtha exports have been heavily disrupted, recently running at around half their pre-war levels. Qatar, the UAE and Iraq are also offering oil from ports outside Hormuz.
